steps.name: Paired differential expression: treated vs control, blocked by subject
caveats: With only 5 pairs, statistical power is limited; treat nominally significant but borderline FDR genes as suggestive, not definitive
Confirm metadata column names (subject, condition) match exactly what the tool reads before building the design formula — do not assume a specific encoding without checking the file
Do not silently drop the pairing structure and run an unpaired t-test/Wald test — that discards the paired design's main statistical advantage and inflates variance
steps.question: Within the 5 paired subjects (control vs treated blood samples), which genes are significantly differentially expressed when the paired/subject structure is modeled explicitly (design ~ subject + condition)?
constraints: Must use a paired/blocked design (subject + condition), not an unpaired two-group comparison
Must probe for DESeq2/edgeR availability before use; do not assume presence
acceptance_criteria: Script loads counts.csv (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata.csv (10 rows: subject, condition) and confirms sample-column-to-metadata-row correspondence by name matching, not positional assumption
Before modeling, the script probes for DESeq2 in R; if unavailable, probes edgeR; if neither is importable, the step reports this explicitly rather than failing silently

Differential expression model design includes subject as a blocking/paired factor and condition (control vs treated) as the factor of interest — e.g. ~ subject + condition in DESeq2, or a paired design matrix in edgeR (model.matrix(~subject+condition))
Low-count genes are filtered prior to dispersion estimation (e.g. minimum count/CPM threshold across samples) given the modest 12000-gene panel
Output includes a full results table with gene symbol, log2FoldChange, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value (FDR) for every tested gene
Output flags genes significant at FDR < 0.05, sorted by adjusted p-value, and reports how many genes pass this threshold
A diagnostic (dispersion plot or MA plot, and a PCA/paired-difference plot showing subjects cluster by pairing) is generated to visually confirm paired structure is behaving as expected
Sample size (n=5 pairs) and its limited statistical power are stated explicitly in the step's textual output

steps.name: Functional enrichment of treatment-responsive genes
caveats: No gene-set reference store was found provisioned at planning time; if still absent at execution time, report the gap rather than skip silently or substitute an unrelated organism's gene sets
Do not treat enrichment p-values as confirmatory — the input gene list already carries the paired analysis's limited power
steps.question: What biological pathways or GO terms are enriched among the genes significantly altered by treatment (from the paired subject+condition DE test)?
constraints: Must use human (Homo sapiens) gene sets only, matching the dataset organism
acceptance_criteria: Uses the full DE results table from T1S1 (not just top N by fold-change) for a ranked/GSEA-style enrichment, and separately the FDR<0.05 gene list for an over-representation test, so results do not depend on an arbitrary cutoff alone

Confirms availability of organism-matched (Homo sapiens) gene set collections (e.g. GO, Hallmark, Reactome) in the environment before running; if none are found, the step reports this gap explicitly instead of fabricating enrichment results
Reports enriched terms with adjusted p-values (FDR) and the overlapping gene sets for each term
States explicitly that enrichment results are exploratory hypothesis-generating output given the n=5 paired design feeding into the DE list

plan.title: Paired within-subject DE analysis, control vs treated
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq raw counts (12000 genes x 10 samples) from 5 subjects, each contributing one control and one treated blood sample — a paired design. The research question ('which genes respond to treatment within each subject') calls for a paired differential expression test that models subject as a blocking factor to remove inter-subject variability and isolate the treatment effect, rather than an unpaired two-group comparison. Step 1 performs QC and paired DE testing using a count-based model with subject + condition design (DESeq2 preferred, edgeR as fallback if DESeq2 is unavailable, confirmed by probing the sandbox before running). Step 2 takes the resulting ranked gene list/DE table and runs functional enrichment (GO/pathway) to interpret the biological programs altered by treatment, using organism-matched (human) gene sets if available in the environment, and reporting explicitly if such reference gene sets are absent so interpretation is not silently skipped.
